: JUDGMENT :
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the common Arbitral Award dated 03.11.2020 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/07/2014-15 pertaining to Sy.No.13/4, 13/5 and 13/6 by respondent No.2.
.2.
In the petition it is stated that National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of the Parliament, "the National Highways Authority of A.P. No.47/2021 India Act, 1988" .

entities.text: National Highways Authority of A.P. No.47/2021 India Act, 1988
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matters connected thereto.

.3. It is stated that the Central Government for the purpose of widening / upgradation maintenance,
management and operation of NH-7 on the stretch of land from kms. 524.720 to kms. 556.840 of Hyderabad - Bengaluru Section issued preliminary notification dated 09.12.2009 under Section 3-A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in-respect of acquisition of lands situated at Sonnappanahalli village,
Bengaluru North Taluka.

The final notification was published in the official Gazette on 30.07.2010.
.4.

It is stated that under the said notification for the 2nd stage of acquisition agricultural (dry) lands in Sy.No. 13/4 to an extent of 150 Sq. Mtrs, Sy. No.13/5 to an extent of 75 Sq. Mtrs., and Sy.No.13/6 to an extent of 75 Sq. Mtrs, situated at the said village belonging to the respondent No. 1 were also acquired.
It A.P. No.47/2021 is stated that the respondent No. 3 was appointed as the competent authority by the Central Government.
.5. It is stated that the respondent No.3 vide award dated 02.04.2011 determined the market value of Agricultural lands at Rs.7,207/- per sq. Mtr.
The respondent No. 3 observed that the average of the sale statistics of Agricultural lands was Rs. 2,91,66,640/- per acre and the guidance value was Rs. 2,000,000/- per acre.

Since both the average of the sales statistics was higher than the guidance value, the respondent No. 3 relied upon the sale statistics value as the market value at Rs.2,91,66,640/- per acre equivalent to Rs.7,207/- per Sq. Mtr.
Being dissatisfied with the amounts awarded by Respondent No.3, the 1 st Respondent approached the 2nd Respondent under Section 3-G(5) of the NH Act.

A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
2 .6.
It is stated that the petitioner entered appearance and filed its Statement of objections with documents as well as written submissions with several Judgments in support of its defence.
The 2 nd A.P. No.47/2021 Respondent without application of mind and proper appreciation of facts,
passed an Arbitral award and redetermined the market value at Rs. 12,973/- per sq. Mtr. for the lands acquired in the 2nd stage of acquisition.
The respondent No. 2 thus enhanced the compensation from Rs. 7,207/- per sq. Mtr to Rs. 12,973/- per sq. feet without according any reasons.
The 2nd Respondent also awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a on the enhanced compensation amount from the date of taking possession of the subject lands till actual deposit.

For the purpose of enhancement of compensation, the respondent No. 2 has relied upon the notification dated 26.09.2011, while the date of Preliminary Notification in case of the subject acquisition in Sonnappanahalli Village was 09th December 2009.

A.P. No.47/2021 (d) The respondent No.2 has not relied upon the Notification which came into effect after a lapse of 1  year from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification and the same is not in accordance with Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
The impugned arbitral award is erroneous on the face it which renders the same patently illegal;

(e) The respondent No. 2 without any justification, in the operative portion of the impugned Arbitral award has added 75% on Rs.3 Crores and redetermined the compensation at Rs.5,25,00,000/- per acre equivalent to Rs.12,973/- per Sq. Mtr.
(f) That several arbitration cases pertaining to Kadiganahalli Village adjacent to Sonnappanahalli Village were disposed of by the very same Arbitrator wherein the market value of NA Lands was A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
3 fixed as Rs. 1314/- per Sq. ft. by the 3rd Respondent.
In such cases, the 2nd Respondent had enhanced the market value from Rs.1,314/- per Sq. ft to Rs.1,500/- per Sq. ft. and there was no further addition of 75% on the same.
Since Kadaginahalli Village is near to Sonnappanahalli Village.
The 2nd A.P. No.47/2021 respondent could not have ignored the said rate and further added 75% on the same in arbitrary manner.
(g) No procedure was decided or set down by the respondent No. 2 before the commencement of the proceedings.

(h) The respondent No. 2 has given the benefit of enhancement to the respondent No. 1 without production by the respondent No. 1 of any records or evidence in support of such enhancement which is completely arbitrary.

(i) The respondent No. 2 has not assigned any reasons for re-determining the compensation amount at Rs. 12,973/- per sq. Mtr. when the parties had neither agreed that no reasons were to be given nor the impugned arbitral award is an award on agreed terms under Section 30 of the A & C Act.

(j) The respondent No. 2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24, nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the A.P. No.47/2021 impugned arbitral award opposed to settled position of law on all the three counts.
(h) The petitioner submits that the impugned arbitral award was passed on 03.11.2020.
The certified copy of the impugned arbitral award was received by the petitioner on 24.12.2020.
The Corrigendum was passed on 18.12.2020.
Hence, the petition is in time.
.8. The respondent No.1 has filed objections admitting Para 1 to 11 and has denied the other averment.
It is stated that the respondent No.2 rightly held that the award of Respondent No.2 is lesser than the market value, based on the present availability of land.
The Arbitrator award is speaking order.
Hence there was no violation on the side of respondent No.2 in enhancing award from Rs.7,207/- per Sq. ft to Rs.12,973/- per Sq.ft.
Even Petitioner itself has not filed application before Arbitrator under Sec. 24 of A& C Act.
Hence it is clear that the impugned arbitral award is not opposed to settled position of law.
That the suit A.P. No.47/2021 filed by the Plaintiff is hit by the provisions of Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.
Hence the suit liable to be dismissed as barred by limitation since the suit is filed after the lapse of 5 months.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the Arbitration suit.

.9. Perused the written arguments filed by Respondent No.1 and citation filed by both sides.
.10.

The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) Whether petitioner in A.P. No.47/2021 has made out sufficient grounds under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act to set aside the arbitral award dated 03.11.2020 passed by respondent No. 2?
A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
4
(2) What order or award?

.11. My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the negative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
A.P. No.47/2021 REASONS .12.
POINT No.1: The 3rd respondent had acquired Sy.No.13/4 to an extent of 120 Sq. mtrs sy.no.13/5 to an extent of 75 meters,
Sy.No.13/6 to an extent of 75 Sq. meters situated at Sonnappanahalli village belonging to the 1st respondent.
The 3rd respondent had fixed market value at Rs.7207/- per sq. meter.
The 1st respondent being aggrieved had approached the 2nd respondent under Sec. 3-G(S) of NH Act.
The 2nd respondent had re-determining market value at Rs.12,973/- per sq. meter.

Being aggrieved by the said award the petitioner has approached this Court under Sec. 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.
.13. Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provide the circumstances under which an award can be set aside by a civil Court.
(2) It is in conflict with contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian Law or iii) It is in conflict with most basic notion of morality or justice.

A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
5 Explanation 2.
The test as to whether there is contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not A.P. No.47/2021 entail a review on the merits of the dispute.

2A It may also be set aside if the Court finds the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of award provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of law or by re appreciation of evidence.
.14.

In Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142, it has been held that:
"From a catena of other judgments of this Court, it is clear that for the objector /
appellant in order to succeed in their challenge against an arbitral award, they must show that the award of the Arbitrator suffered from perversity or an error of law or that the Arbitrator has otherwise misconducted himself.

entities.text: Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely showing that there is another reasonable interpretation or possible view on the basis of the material on the record is insufficient to allow for the interference by the Court."
Bearing in mind the above section and decision, now it has to be seen whether the impugned award A.P. No.47/2021 suffers from any patent error, illegality as envisaged above.
.15. The petitioner has contended that Arbitrator has relied upon the notification dated 21.09.2011 and it was published on 26.09.2011.

Preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 09.12.2009.
.16.

It is stated that as per the Substantive Law NH Authority Act Section 3-G(7)(a) the Arbitrator while determining the amount shall take into consideration the market value of the land as on the date of publication of the notification under Section 3-A of NH Act.
The respondent No. 2 could not have relied upon the notification which came into effect after lapse of 1 and  years from the date of preliminary notification.
No reasons has been assigned by the Arbitrator for considering notification.

.17. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
A.P. No.47/2021 "if the award is contrary to the Substantive provisions of law or the provisions of the Act or against the terms of the contract, it would be patently illegal,
which could be interfered under Section 34".

entities.text: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above decision applies to the case on hand.

The Arbitrator relying upon guidance value dated 26.09.2011 has fixed the market value at Rs.
A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
6 5,25,00,000/- per acre for agricultural land.
Even if he relied he ought to have deescalated the value to bring it to the date of notification.

It is clear that the respondent No. 2 Arbitrator has ignored the Substantive Law under Section 3-G(7)(a) of National Highways Authority Act and thereby the provisions of Section 28 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act while passing the impugned award.

Therefore, the award is patently illegal.
.18.
The Arbitrator has relied upon estimated market value of the immovable properties and buildings for registration in Bengaluru dated 21.09.2011.
This A.P. No.47/2021 document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
.19.

As an Arbitrator has relied on the estimated market value of immovable properties and buildings dated 21.09.2011 for Registration in Bengaluru without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So there is patent illegality.
The petitioner has contended that respondent No. 2 had failed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
On perusal of arbitral records it is seen that after issue of notice opportunity has been given to the parties to file their claim statement.
The claimant has filed claim statement.
The respondent has filed written statement.
Both parties filed written arguments.
The case was posted for orders.
So, it cannot be said that opportunity was not given to the petitioner herein to have their say.

.21. The petitioner has contended that the respondent No. 2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation amount at Rs. 12,973/- per sq. feet; that he has not assigned any reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 26.09.2011.
.22.

As per the notification the market value of agricultural lands abutting to NH is mentioned at Sl.
No.67.
In the said Sl. No. Sy. No.13 is mentioned.
The A.P. No.47/2021 market value of agricultural land is mentioned as Rs.300 lakhs.
The 2nd respondent has added 75% on Rs. 300 lakhs and redetermined the compensation at Rs.5,25,00,000/- per acre = Rs.12,373 per Sq. meter.
The 2nd respondent has not stated the reason for providing 75% enhanced compensation.

.23. Section 3(G) of the National High Ways Act, mandatorily provides that, the competent authority or the Arbitrator to take into consideration the factors mentioned in Sub clause (a) to (d) while determining the market value of the compensation payable in-respect of the acquired lands.
But neither the award nor the order sheet shows any materials on record as to how he had followed the said provision.

A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
7 .24.

In Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC) has held that:
"Reasons must be indicated in the award as that would reflect thought process leading to a particular conclusion.

entities.text: Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
To satisfy the requirement of Section 31(3), the reasons must be stated A.P. No.47/2021 by the Arbitral Tribunal upon which the award is based; want of reasons would make such award legally flawed."
.25.

The counsel for the respondent No.1 has contended that the arbitration has rightly observed that the acquired land is agricultural dry in nature capable of being used for commercial and industrial purposes; that the acquired land is attached to National Highway, prima-facie suitable for all commercial purposes and no document is required for passing enhancement.
On perusal of the arbitration award it is seen that no where the arbitrator has stated that the lands are suitable for commercial and industrial purpose.

.26. The respondent has contended that the compensation awarded by the SLAO is less than the present market value and so the arbitrator has enhanced the compensation at the rate of 75% and 9% interest has been fixed as per Sec. 3-H (5) of NH Act 1956.
No document was placed by respondent No.1 to show that the market value was higher than what was awarded by 3rd respondent.
The respondent No.1 has relied upon the Judgment in A.S.No.82/2018 and A.S. No.56/2018.
The said Judgment pertain to acquisition in respect Mulabagilu - Kolar, Bangalore section.
The acquisition in the present case pertain to Bangalore North Taluk whereas the acquisition in the above two judgments pertain to Bangalore East Taluk, Apart from that notification are different.
So the above judgments are not applicable to the case on hand.
.28. The respondent No. 1 has contended that the above petition is barred by limitation.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court had directed in sue moto case extension of the period of limitation in all proceedings before the Court from 15.03.2020 till 28.02.2022.
In view of the above decision the petition is in time.

.29. On perusal of the records and the award of the Arbitrator it is seen that the respondent No.2 has not decided the dispute in accordance with Section A.P. No.47/2021 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral Award opposed to settled position of law.
.30.
The respondent has brought to the notice of the Court that the 3rd respondent has paid enhancement of compensation in respect of Sy. No. 8/1 extent 1500 Sq. metrs of Sonnappanahalli village.
The land in the said case has been acquired under the same notification of the present case and common award has been passed by the 2nd respondent.
As lands in Sy.No. 8/1 cannot be far away from Sy.No. 13/4, 13/5 and 13/6.
The petitioner having paid the enhanced compensation in respect of Smt. Nagamma has to award same compensation to the petitioner in the present case.

A.P./47/2021 on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30478892/
8 .31.

It is also relevant to note that the second respondent has paid enhancement of compensation in respect of Sy.No. 12/1, 12/2 and 12/3 measuring to an extent of 2152, 538,1076 Sq.ft respectively of A.P. No.47/2021 Sonnappanahalli village.
The said lands have been acquired under the same notification under which the present case land has also been acquired.
Common order has been passed in this case and in the case of Sy. No.12/1, 12/2 and 12/3.
The only difference is that the said lands are non-agricultural lands.
The second respondent has relied upon the same notification and has granted 75% more than the market value fixed in the guidelines.
The petitioner having paid the enhanced compensation in respect of Sy.No.12/1, 12/2 and 12/3 will have to pay the same compensation to the claimant.
.32. Though the Arbitrator has not complied with Section 28(1)(a) and Sec.31 (3) of A & C Act.
Endeavor of the Court should be honour and support the award as far as possible.

The petitioner and the 3rd respondent having honoured award passed by the 2 nd respondent in respect of Sy.No.8/1, 12/1, 12/2 and 12/3 has to honour the same in case to the respondent No.1 also as common award has been passed.
The respondent No. 1 cannot be treated differently.
For the said reason I do A.P. No.47/2021 not intend to interfere with the award passed by the respondent No.2.
Hence, I answer point No.1 in the negative.
.33. Point No.2:

In view of the aforesaid finding on point No.1 I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER A.P. No.47/2021 is dismissed.

The common impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 in so far as pertaining to case No.LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR.53/2012-2013 in-respect of Sy.No.13/4 acquired to an extent of 150 sq. mtrs, Sy.No.13/5 acquired to an extent of 75 Sq. Mtrs and Sy.No.13/6 acquired to an extent of 75 Sq. Metrs.
Read with Corrigendum dated 18th December 2020 is confirmed.
